# AI Chips & Data Centres Daily
> **More than ten thousand jobs ride on TSMC's Arizona expansion groundbreaking December fourth.**

**What You Need to Know:** More than ten thousand direct jobs are attached to the expansion groundbreaking President Donald Trump is set to attend on December fourth at TSMC’s Phoenix site, where twelve thousand to fifteen thousand construction and support workers are already on the ground. Huawei and ChangXin Memory Technologies have papers on the February ISSCC draft program, including a high-bandwidth memory design US media describe as twice the data-pin density of Samsung and SK hynix parts now in mass production. Nvidia has told Dell and Supermicro to stop shipping servers into Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia under last week’s US licence rules.

### Top Story
President Donald Trump will attend a groundbreaking on December fourth for an expansion of TSMC’s semiconductor plant in Phoenix, a company spokesperson confirmed, and Bloomberg reported a White House official expects TSMC executives plus supplier and customer representatives at the ceremony. Whether Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang attends has not been decided. TSMC already manufactures Nvidia’s Blackwell chips, and chips for AMD and Apple, at the first Arizona plant. The White House official said the expansion is expected to create more than ten thousand direct jobs once completed, and that twelve thousand to fifteen thousand construction and support workers are currently at the site. TSMC first announced the Arizona plant near the end of Trump’s first administration and, in March last year, unveiled a one hundred sixty-five billion dollar US investment plan to expand advanced semiconductor production in the country. The December fourth event is a groundbreaking for the expansion, not an energized new fab. Source: [biz.chosun.com](https://biz.chosun.com/en/en-it/2026/11/26/FVJ6OVBMQBEMJB2M7QJL4S4ZCE/)
Source: [yahoo.com](https://www.yahoo.com/news/videos/president-trump-visit-phoenix-tsmc-012817272.html)

### Silicon
**China's Chipmakers Step Up Efforts to Catch Samsung Electronics and SK hynix: Fnnews**
IEEE’s draft program for the International Solid-State Circuits Conference, set for San Francisco next February, previews papers from Huawei and ChangXin Memory Technologies. Huawei plans to present next-generation high-bandwidth memory; US media reported the data-pin density is twice that of products Samsung Electronics and SK hynix currently have in mass production, a design that in theory would raise memory bandwidth. CXMT will show next-generation DDR5 and a paper on the LPDDR6 interface. Earlier this month CXMT said it had completed engineering-sample validation of a sixth-generation DRAM platform on a 4F2 cell and claimed it was first to finish that validation. Nikkei Asia reported Samsung and SK hynix agreed, through a patent cross-licence, to adopt some of Yangtze Memory Technologies’ Xtacking-related stacking technology for 3D NAND. A memory-industry official said the deals are mainly to avoid legal disputes after YMTC filed broadly, and that YMTC’s approach has also made it less exposed to US controls on advanced manufacturing equipment, with some leading firms now licensing the technology. Source: [en.fnnews.com](https://en.fnnews.com/news/202611261821552363)

**Weimob Spends Over CNY 400 Million Buying 5,000 NVIDIA RTX PRO 5500 Blackwell GPUs: BigGo Finance**
Weimob Group said on the twenty-sixth that wholly owned Weimob Zhisuan signed two independent GPU purchases, for five thousand Nvidia RTX PRO 5500 Blackwell processors, at about four hundred thirty million yuan, roughly sixty-four point six million dollars. Ingram Micro is supplying four thousand units for about three hundred forty-four million yuan, about fifty-one point seven million dollars, and Shanghai Fuxin one thousand units for eighty-six point five million yuan, about thirteen million dollars. Both sellers are independent third parties, and neither deal is conditional on the other. Weimob said the cards go first to multimodal, image and video generation for its own AI products, then some idle capacity may be leased to other enterprises. It said tight GPU supply led it to split the buy across suppliers. Source: [finance.biggo.com](https://finance.biggo.com/news/7032f488-ed4f-4c95-a6fd-d78470f7db0e)

**SK Hynix seeks TSMC 3nm expertise as Micron steps up hiring: digitimes**
Digitimes reports SK hynix is seeking engineers with experience on TSMC’s 3-nanometer process to develop customized high-bandwidth memory, while Micron is increasing hiring in South Korea to support its Asian expansion. Source: [digitimes.com](https://www.digitimes.com/news/a20261126VL224/sk-hynix-tsmc-micron-3nm-hbm.html)

**NVIDIA Cuts RTX 50-Series Supply as RTX 60-Series Faces Possible Delay: TechPowerUp**
Board Channels, via TechPowerUp, reports Nvidia has told add-in-card partners they will get twenty to thirty percent fewer gaming GPUs over the next three months, November 2026 through January 2027. The post is about China. Taiwan’s Commercial Times, citing Taiwanese ODMs, reported new B300 orders take twenty-six to forty weeks and GB300 about fourteen to twenty-six weeks, with RTX Pro cards and DGX Station stretched past that. Industry sources expect wafers freed by the GeForce cut to move toward data-centre chips. These are trade-press reports, not a Nvidia shipment notice. Source: [techpowerup.com](https://www.techpowerup.com/355196/nvidia-cuts-rtx-50-series-supply-as-rtx-60-series-faces-possible-delay-per-reports)

### Data Centres & Power
**MCRPS Power Supply for Enterprise Data Centers: EE Times**
Infineon has a 5.6-kilowatt MCRPS reference design aimed at next-generation common redundant power supplies in enterprise servers. Source: [eetimes.com](https://www.eetimes.com/mcrps-power-supply-for-enterprise-data-centers/)

### Supply Chain & Policy
**Nvidia faces mounting scrutiny as export controls disrupt chip shipments: National Technology News**
Nvidia has told manufacturing partners Dell and Supermicro to stop shipping servers to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia, the Financial Times reported, citing three people familiar with the matter, after last week’s US rules on cloud access to restricted processors. It is unclear whether the stop is temporary. Providers have ninety days to obtain licences by showing restricted entities are not end users. Nvidia recorded one hundred four billion dollars of revenue through its Singapore subsidiary in 2025, up seventy-two percent on the prior year. Lenders have halted about five hundred million dollars of credit for Singapore cloud provider Aolani’s planned computing arrangement with ByteDance. S&P Global Ratings put Nvidia’s AA rating on downgrade watch, warning a one-notch cut could follow within ninety days; Moody’s kept Aa1 with a stable outlook. Source: [nationaltechnology.co.uk](https://nationaltechnology.co.uk/Nvidia_Faces_Mounting_Scrutiny_As_Export_Controls_Disrupt_Chip_Shipments.php)
Source: [ft.com](https://www.ft.com/content/7838a715-07d4-4605-aa60-21f5af2b2370?syn-25a6b1a6=1)
Source: [straitstimes.com](https://www.straitstimes.com/world/united-states/nvidia-halts-server-shipments-to-four-south-east-asian-countries-including-singapore-report)

**Congress to Investigate Jensen Huang, Tighten Chip Controls: Domino Theory**
Jensen Huang and Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter are due next week before three House committees and the Senate Banking Committee. Senator Chuck Schumer wrote that Huang shipped extremely advanced chips to China in violation of export-control law. Representative Hakeem Jeffries has called for export-control legislation in next year’s defense bill. Senator Elizabeth Warren said Huang’s return increases the urgency of passing bipartisan export-control bills. Three Republican members of the House Foreign Affairs Committee said the board’s brief investigation and reinstatement do not erase the national-security questions. President Trump said he personally convinced the board to rehire Huang. Bill Bishop wrote that Trump may ignore new statutes the way he set aside the TikTok law. Chris McGuire said legislation still on the table does not force licence denials in named circumstances. Derek Scissors said veto-proof legislation is easier in next year’s Democratic-controlled Congress, and that the open question is whether that Congress treats export controls as a priority. Source: [dominotheory.com](https://dominotheory.com/congress-to-investigate-jensen-huang-tighten-chip-controls/)

**SIA Applauds Introduction of Bipartisan Legislation to Extend Semiconductor Investment Credit: Semiconductor Digest**
The Semiconductor Industry Association welcomed bipartisan legislation to extend the semiconductor investment tax credit, which is currently set to expire at the end of 2026. Source: [semiconductor-digest.com](https://www.semiconductor-digest.com/sia-applauds-introduction-of-bipartisan-legislation-to-extend-semiconductor-investment-credit/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=rss&utm_campaign=sia-applauds-introduction-of-bipartisan-legislation-to-extend-semiconductor-investment-credit)

### The Teardown: Years of Capacity Against Months of Permission
A supply commitment is a dated promise to take wafers, memory and buildings that do not exist yet. Longbridge, reading Nvidia’s CFO commentary, puts those supply and capacity commitments at three hundred ninety billion dollars. About two hundred three billion dollars falls in fiscal 2028, roughly February 2027 through January 2028, and about ninety-two billion dollars in fiscal 2029. Together that is about three quarters of the book. Inventory has risen to thirty-nine point seven billion dollars. The bottleneck Longbridge describes is no longer the processor alone. SK hynix said in October 2026 that, counting long-term agreements and demand still under negotiation, its DRAM and high-bandwidth memory output through 2029 is largely booked, and Nvidia’s commitments grew mainly through multi-year memory purchases. Power and credit sit on the same timeline. Nvidia has guarantees tied to customers’ and partners’ land, power, buildings and systems, with maximum gross exposure of one hundred eighteen billion dollars. Its neocloud agreements carry financing, deployment and acceptance conditions. The International Energy Agency’s Energy and AI outlook, as Longbridge cites it, projects data-centre electricity use of about nine hundred forty-five terawatt-hours by 2030, and says about twenty percent of planned projects could be delayed by grid constraints.

Walk the commitment book without treating it as cash already spent. Start at three hundred ninety billion dollars. Fiscal 2028’s two hundred three billion and fiscal 2029’s ninety-two billion add to two hundred ninety-five billion, the three-quarter slice that sits two fiscal years out. The nearer quarter is real, but the commentary Longbridge uses does not split it by quarter, so it stays an unnamed remainder. The one hundred eighteen billion dollars of guarantees is a different stack. It is not a purchase order for HBM. It is a backstop on land, power, buildings and systems, and it is gross exposure, a ceiling, not a forecast of what will be drawn. Acceptance conditions matter because a neocloud that cannot take delivery does not convert a guarantee into a running cluster. The twenty percent figure is a project-delay share in the IEA projection, not a slice of the one hundred eighteen billion. Multiplying them would invent a loss the source never calculated. What the two numbers do show, side by side, is that chip commitments can be fully placed while a fifth of the buildings those chips were meant to fill are still waiting on a grid connection. Memory makes the same split in time: a book through 2029 at SK hynix is a physical allocation, and it does not move if the building slips.

That guarantee-for-the-shell choice stops being the right tool when the thing that fails is not the customer’s ability to finance a building. Longbridge’s own observation is that commitments are counted in years while recent policy windows are counted in months: the latest US-China truce extension was only two months, and the export rules carry a sixty-day comment period. A prepayment to a memory supplier, which management told Tom’s Hardware it may offer, clears a supply queue. It does not clear a licence, and it does not energize a substation. When the binding limit is who may lawfully use the compute, or whether the interconnect arrives before the acceptance window, the one hundred eighteen billion dollars of building guarantees is aimed at the constraint that is no longer the one in front of the cluster. Source: [longbridge.com](https://longbridge.com/en/academy/ai-investing/blog/what-three-tests-does-the-ai-chip-supply-chain-face-in-2026-earnings-us-export-rules-and-us-china-ties-101709)

### On the Horizon
- The US-China truce Longbridge cites expires on 10 January 2027.
- The Bureau of Industry and Security interim rule on remote access to advanced semiconductors, published in the Federal Register on 19 November 2026, stays open for comment until 19 January 2027.
- Huawei and CXMT presentations on the ISSCC draft program are set for San Francisco next February.
- The semiconductor investment tax credit SIA wants extended is currently set to expire at the end of 2026.

# AI Chips & Data Centres Daily
> **Samsung plans fivefold Xi'an V9 NAND growth, to fifty thousand wafers, for AI SSDs.**

**What You Need to Know:** Samsung is planning to lift 286-layer V9 NAND at its Xi'an X2 fab from about 10,000 wafers a month to about 50,000 by the end of 2027, aimed at enterprise SSDs for AI data centers. Chinese cloud buyers are cutting 2027 memory orders, and TrendForce now puts that year's NAND revenue near $419.3 billion and DRAM revenue at $1.15 trillion. In Phoenix, a utility contract would take TSMC toward 1.88 gigawatts.

### Top Story
Samsung is planning a large internal conversion of V9 NAND at its second Xi'an fab, not a new factory, TechPowerUp reports from Seoul Economic Daily and industry sources. The X2 line now turns out about 10,000 300 mm wafers a month of 286-layer V9; the plan is about 50,000 by the end of 2027, aimed at enterprise SSDs for AI data centers. An electroplating line would go into empty cleanroom space, with equipment moving in around February 2027 and the conversion finished by November 2027, while 20% to 30% of the fab's existing V6 line would also switch to V9. Samsung has previously denied claims of expanding production capacity, so the report reads as a reshuffle inside an existing fab even as the wafer count rises sharply. NAND spot prices have already started falling. Source: [techpowerup.com](https://www.techpowerup.com/355189/samsung-doubles-down-on-v9-nand-in-china)

### Silicon
**Cuts to Chinese CSP Demand Expecting to Slow Memory Industry Revenue Growth in 2027: TechPowerUp**
TrendForce says Chinese cloud service providers have reduced their 2027 memory orders, putting downward pressure on the industry price outlook. NAND Flash is expected to enter a downward pricing cycle as supply keeps expanding, and TrendForce has lowered its 2027 NAND Flash revenue forecast to about US$419.3 billion. DRAM is still expected to stay undersupplied, but quarterly price increases are projected to moderate. That revision takes the 2027 DRAM revenue forecast down to $1.15 trillion. Source: [techpowerup.com](https://www.techpowerup.com/355192/cuts-to-chinese-csp-demand-expecting-to-slow-memory-industry-revenue-growth-in-2027)

**Intel Wins Microsoft Packaging Order but Hits '35% Yield' Wall in Bid to Enter Google TPU Supply Chain: BigGo Finance**
BigGo Finance reports that Intel has won a Microsoft packaging order. The same report says a 35% yield wall is in the way of a bid to enter the Google TPU supply chain. Source: [finance.biggo.com](https://finance.biggo.com/news/4c3938a8-4ed6-4b6e-b719-fdcc8d22c072)

**LOTA caches data on GPU nodes at up to 7 GB/s per GPU: CoreWeave**
CoreWeave says robotics data is 3D scenes and sensor streams, and a single physical AI program can generate petabytes of it, reread throughout training. On CoreWeave, LOTA, the Local Object Transport Accelerator, caches that data on GPU nodes at up to 7 GB/s per GPU so the GPUs train instead of waiting on reads. The post says the pieces then have to run as one loop. Source: [x.com](https://x.com/CoreWeave/status/2125367694639743440)

### Data Centres & Power
**TSMC Arizona offers a look at what could come to Brazos County: KBTX**
TSMC's north Phoenix campus is under construction toward a contracted load of about 1.88 gigawatts, KBTX reports, with the first fab already in production since late 2024. Arizona Public Service signed a direct pricing contract on October 16 to ramp service to about 1.88 gigawatts for fabs and advanced packaging over an initial 25-year term. Engineers at the site's water resource center say the campus uses 4.75 million gallons of water a day, mostly reclaimed wastewater plus a small amount of groundwater, all through the City of Phoenix, and TSMC says it recycles 65% of intake, about 3.5 million gallons a day. Arizona's Family, cited by KBTX, put the first fab at about 5,300 acre-feet a year, roughly 1.7 billion gallons, enough for about 15,000 Phoenix households; Sarah Porter of Arizona State University's Kyl Center estimated about 15% or slightly more evaporates. The campus also makes nearly 15 megawatts of solar on site, with panels doubling as covered parking for about 4,000 vehicles. The first three fabs are estimated to employ 6,000 people, up from about 3,500; the county lists the project as an active Title V air-permit source; the 2025 sustainability report says most pollutants were reduced 95% or more and volatile organic compounds by 98.9%; and TSMC says it recycles 96% of waste, with less than 1% reaching a landfill. Source: [kbtx.com](https://www.kbtx.com/2026/11/24/tsmc-arizona-offers-look-what-could-come-brazos-county/)

**Google plans 1.2GW data center near Châteauroux, France: Data Center Dynamics**
Google has announced a data-center plan near Châteauroux, France, and Data Center Dynamics reports a connection request for a second data center in the area. The headline states 1.2GW while the story URL reads 12GW, so the capacity unit in the visible text is ambiguous. Source: [datacenterdynamics.com](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/google-planning-12gw-data-center-near-ch%C3%A2teauroux-france-report/)

### Supply Chain & Policy
**US lawmakers from both parties pressure Nvidia, call for tighter chip export controls on China: Zaobao**
Zaobao, citing Reuters, reports that Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer wrote on X on Tuesday, November 24, that Jensen Huang shipping highly advanced chips to China was akin to selling rocket engines to the Soviet Union during the space race, and alleged a violation of US export-control laws. Republican Senator Dave McCormick said Congress must get to the bottom of what happened and then strengthen export controls so China cannot reach the most advanced chips through a back door. Democratic Representatives Frank Pallone, Gregory Meeks, Jamie Raskin and Robert Garcia wrote to President Donald J. Trump asking how much he knew about ties between Huang and suspected Chinese government agents, requesting administration correspondence with Nvidia's board, and asking whether a personal relationship had influenced the handling. Senate Banking Committee chairman Tim Scott said Huang would attend a public hearing on December 3; a closed-door briefing by three House committees is expected on December 1. Republican Representative Pat Harrigan said reinstating Huang as chief executive at this time was inappropriate and sent a dangerous signal. Zaobao notes its English text is an AI translation and that the original Chinese remains authoritative. Source: [zaobao.com.sg](https://www.zaobao.com.sg/en/news/world/us-lawmakers-both-parties-pressure-nvidia-call-tighter-chip-export-controls-china)

**TSMC tax break application heads to governor and school district: KBTX**
One day after the filing, Deputy Comptroller Noah Betz signed a recommendation on November 24 that TSMC meets Jobs, Energy, Technology and Innovation eligibility for a Brazos County logic plant at 2-nanometer or better. The comptroller's report estimates a $354 million school property-tax break over 20 years, while the project would still generate about $405 million in school operating taxes in that time; those figures are projections, and the state would replace the revenue College Station ISD loses. The break covers maintenance-and-operations taxes for 10 years, not the debt-service portion. The report says the project would need to meet a minimum of 35 jobs at a required wage of at least $73,603. One no from the governor or the district stops the deal, and the project remains subject to a final investment decision. Source: [kbtx.com](https://www.kbtx.com/2026/11/24/tsmc-tax-break-application-heads-governor-school-district/)

### Also Today
**Taipower to pour NT$109.6 billion into grid for TSMC-led chip boom in southern Taiwan: digitimes**
Digitimes reports Taipower will put NT$109.6 billion into the grid for a TSMC-led chip expansion in southern Taiwan. Source: [digitimes.com](https://www.digitimes.com/news/a20261125PD217/taiwan-power-company-taiwan-expansion-infrastructure-transmission.html)

**HBM Prices to More Than Double with Big Tech Entry: Chosun**
Chosun reports HBM prices are set to more than double as Big Tech enters the market. Source: [chosun.com](https://www.chosun.com/english/industry-en/2026/11/25/MJRWY4RHTFD5ZELSZNQ7FCE3H4/)

**Winbond Widens Edge AI Reach, Certifies NOR Flash: EE Times**
EE Times reports Winbond has certified NOR flash while widening its edge AI memory reach. Source: [eetimes.com](https://www.eetimes.com/winbond-widens-edge-ai-reach-certifies-nor-flash/)

**Singapore, US work on mechanism for chip export control: Singapore Business Review**
Singapore Business Review reports Singapore and the United States are working on a mechanism for chip export control. Source: [sbr.com.sg](https://sbr.com.sg/information-technology/news/singapore-us-work-mechanism-chip-export-control)

**US Congress advances three AI chip export bills as CEO returns to Nvidia: digitimes**
Digitimes reports the US Congress is advancing three AI chip export bills as Nvidia's chief executive returns. Source: [digitimes.com](https://www.digitimes.com/news/a20261125PD211/ai-chip-nvidia-chips-equipment.html)

**Chip Industry Technical Paper Roundup: Nov. 25: Semiconductor Engineering**
Semiconductor Engineering's November 25 roundup points to work on hybrid-bonded 3D NAND analog in-memory compute, defect-aware chiplet matching, HBM latency reduction for GPU systems, backside clock meshes, post-quantum hardware verification, CMP virtual metrology, and e-beam stitching losses in silicon-on-insulator waveguides. Source: [semiengineering.com](https://semiengineering.com/chip-industry-technical-paper-roundup-nov-25-2/)

### The Teardown: The Core Count Left in the First Weights
A published weight file still carries a trace of the machine that first filled it. Training does not start from a blank tensor. A library writes an initial pattern, and that pattern is a function of how the initialization kernel was launched: how many streaming multiprocessors took part, and how the random streams were mapped onto them. Israel Defense, reporting a forensic study by Unemploymentlabs, says researchers reconstructed those initial values from publicly released model weights and then searched for the hardware and initialization configurations that reproduce the numbers exactly. The evidence is in the weights themselves, not in a leak or an insider account.

The discriminator they publish is the core count. A Blackwell B200 or B300 signature in this method is 148 streaming multiprocessors. A GB200 or GB300 signature is 152. Six models released since April 2026 by DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, MiniMax and Ant Group contain patterns consistent with Blackwell, while earlier models from the same firms line up with Hopper. DeepSeek-V4-Flash and MiniMax-M3 match the 148-core B200 or B300 pattern. DeepSeek-V4-Pro, Kimi K3, Kimi K3.1-Pro and Ling-3.1-flash match the 152-core GB200 or GB300 pattern. For DeepSeek-V4-Flash and Kimi K3, the match was checked on physical Blackwell chips, not only in a search over configurations. DeepSeek-V3, Kimi K2.5 and Ling-3.0-flash stay on the Hopper side of the same test. Kimi K2.7-Code sits in between: Hopper-era weights, plus a minor portion consistent with B200 or B300. That is a generation change with a date window, not a single ambiguous file.

The control set is the part that makes the count usable. The method was run on 24 models whose developers had already disclosed the hardware. Every one matched the disclosure, including Nvidia's Nemotron-3 Ultra, which showed the same 152-core signature. Israel Defense says those correlations are far stronger than a statistical-chance explanation. The only other configuration the researchers identified that could mimic the pattern is custom-configured AMD hardware, which is itself restricted for export to China. That alternative was ruled out for DeepSeek-V4-Flash and called highly improbable for the other five of the six.

The fingerprint names how the weights were generated. It supports the hypothesis that Blackwell also ran the training, and it does not prove that hypothesis. It also does not say where the chips sat, how access was obtained, or whether an export rule was broken. The design choice — treat a reproduced initialization, verified on silicon for two models and against 24 disclosed cases, as evidence of Blackwell use — stops being the right instrument when the question is a place, a shipment, or a violation, or when a later training stack could have left the initialization's machine behind. At that point the 148-versus-152 split still describes the first fill, and it no longer identifies the training run. Source: [israeldefense.co.il](https://www.israeldefense.co.il/en/node/73236)

### On the Horizon
- College Station ISD holds a public hearing at 5 p.m. on December 10, 2026, at 1812 Welsh Ave., and trustees could vote that day on the JETI agreement.
- Governor Greg Abbott has until December 24, 2026, to decide, and must notify the parties by December 31.
- TSMC's Arizona contract calls for upfront credit support and collateral starting January 1, 2027, backing new APS resources.
- An industrial water reclamation plant at the Phoenix campus is due online in 2028, aimed at lifting reuse from 65% to more than 95%.

# AI Chips & Data Centres Daily
> **Helios racks are powered in Azure labs, giving AMD's next platform a cloud foothold.**

**What You Need to Know:** Helios racks are powered in Microsoft Azure labs, and AMD says Azure is among the first cloud providers bringing that next-generation rack-scale platform to life. A TSMC unit has asked Texas for a property-tax cap on a proposed $22.6 billion Brazos County campus aimed at 2-nanometer or more advanced chips. The same day, Singapore's prime minister said the city is still checking Megaspeed under its own law after the United States moved to blacklist the firm and six affiliates.

### Top Story
AMD says Helios racks are powered in Microsoft labs. The company says it is working side by side with Azure to advance its next-generation rack-scale AI platform. It describes Azure as among the first cloud providers bringing Helios to life. Source: [x.com](https://x.com/AMD/status/2124926480228422077)

### Silicon
**ASRock Industrial Unveils Robotics-in-a-Box to Democratize Physical AI Development: TechPowerUp**
ASRock Industrial launched RBK-100 Robotics-in-a-Box, built around the NUC BOX-358H and the Intel Core Ultra X7 Processor 358H. The box combines local AI computing, an RGB depth camera, a 6-DOF leader-and-follower robotic arm set, and pre-installed AiRoboStarter software. ASRock Industrial says the package is meant for researchers, educators, and developers, and that putting edge compute, vision, manipulation, and software in one platform cuts integration work so users can spend time on model experiments, robotic skills, and physical-AI applications. Source: [techpowerup.com](https://www.techpowerup.com/355151/asrock-industrial-unveils-robotics-in-a-box-to-democratize-physical-ai-development)

**Jetway Intros MTX-RYZ1 Mini-ITX Industrial Board with Ryzen 7 PRO 8845HS: TechPowerUp**
Jetway introduced the MTX-RYZ1 Mini-ITX industrial board around the Ryzen 7 PRO 8845HS, an AMD Hawk Point Zen 4 chip with 8 cores, 16 threads, and a 3.8 GHz base clock, aimed at embedded and industrial systems. Two SO-DIMM slots take up to 96 GB of DDR5-5600, ECC or non-ECC. Storage is two SATA III ports and two M.2 2280 slots at PCIe 4.0 x4, plus an M.2 2230 E-key slot with PCIe x1 and USB 2.0 for wireless, and one PCIe 4.0 x8 slot. Networking is two Intel I226-V 2.5 GbE ports. The board can drive up to four independent displays over DisplayPort, eDP, and LVDS, with DP0 co-laid with eDP and DP1 co-laid with LVDS. Serial I/O is two configurable RS-232/422/485 ports and four RS-232 connections on headers, plus a 16-bit GPIO header, SMBus, four rear USB 3.2 Gen 1 ports, six USB 2.0 ports on headers, a Realtek ALC897 codec, a programmable watchdog, Wake-on-LAN, and TPM 2.0. Source: [techpowerup.com](https://www.techpowerup.com/355148/jetway-intros-mtx-ryz1-mini-itx-industrial-board-with-ryzen-7-pro-8845hs)

### Data Centres & Power
**Sponsored: Bitera completes SOC 2 Type II Audit, strengthening governance to international standards: Data Center Dynamics**
Bitera, a carrier-neutral data center in Jakarta’s Kuningan district, has completed a SOC 2 Type II audit. The same note says the site has maintained 100 percent power availability since opening in 2024. Source: [datacenterdynamics.com](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/product-news/bitera-completes-soc-2-type-ii-audit-strengthening-governance-to-international-standards/)

**JUPITER Remains Among the 5 Fastest Supercomputers and Europe’s No. 1: HPCwire**
JUPITER remains among the five fastest supercomputers in the world and Europe’s most powerful, and it remains the most energy-efficient machine in the exascale class. Two research projects run on JUPITER have been nominated for ACM Gordon Bell Prizes, both with contributions by JSC experts. Source: [hpcwire.com](https://www.hpcwire.com/off-the-wire/jupiter-remains-among-the-5-fastest-supercomputers-and-europes-no-1/)

### Supply Chain & Policy
**TSMC Unit Seeks Texas Tax Concession for Proposed $22.6 Billion Chip Project: MarketScreener**
Beyond earlier aid totals and site talk, a TSMC unit has put a specific Texas plan on a tax application. Digitimes reports TSMC is considering a $22.6 billion semiconductor campus in Texas, including about $14 billion in machinery and equipment, and is weighing Texas against Arizona. Channel NewsAsia, via UA.NEWS, reports the unit applied to the Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts under the Jobs, Energy, Technology and Innovation program for a property-tax cap on a planned Brazos County facility, and called the incentive a decisive factor in the construction decision. The planned complex could cover more than 3,200 acres and include one or more plants plus supporting infrastructure, producing chips at 2-nanometer or more advanced nodes for artificial intelligence, high-performance computing, and mobile devices. The application names Arizona, where the unit has operated a plant since late 2024, as the alternative, and estimates at least 2,099 direct jobs over the next four decades. Taiwan News frames the same Texas plan at NT$743 billion. This is an application and a site under consideration, not an energized fab. Source: [digitimes.com](https://www.digitimes.com/news/a20261124VL226/tsmc-texas-arizona-investment-manufacturing.html) · [ua.news](https://ua.news/en/dovkolo-svitu/virobnik-chipiv-tsmc-prosit-obmezhiti-podatok-dlia-zavodu-v-tekhasi-za-22-6-mlrd-channel-newsasia) · [taiwannews.com.tw](https://www.taiwannews.com.tw/en/news/6480408) · [marketscreener.com](https://www.marketscreener.com/news/tsmc-unit-seeks-texas-tax-concession-for-proposed-22-6-billion-chip-project-ce7851dad080f420)

**S’pore working with US on chip export enforcement as Megaspeed probe continues: PM Wong: Yahoo News Singapore**
On November 23 the US Commerce Department moved to add Megaspeed and six related companies to the Entity List, citing the risk that advanced computing technology is diverted to unauthorized end users or uses. The two other Singapore names are Apex Enterprise Solutions (Singapore) and Swiftdata; the Malaysia names are MSFusion, PT Megaspeed International, and Speedmatrix; the Thailand name is Megaspeed (Thailand). Companies on the list face additional US export licensing requirements, with applications likely to be denied. On November 24 in Canberra, with Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, Prime Minister Lawrence Wong said Singapore does not enforce America’s export controls but does not want to be used as a conduit, and that Singapore is working with the US administration on information sharing and a mechanism so America can do its own enforcement. He said Singapore asked for some information and not all of it was forthcoming, that discussions continue on end users and document checks, and that Singapore’s own question is whether Megaspeed breached Singapore law. The Ministry of Home Affairs has said police and Singapore Customs began investigating several companies, including Megaspeed, and their key officers in February 2025 over possible inaccurate declarations on server purchases. Alice Huang was interviewed in June 2025 and had her passport impounded; in February 2026 police found insufficient evidence on those declarations, issued a stern warning, and barred her from re-entering; MHA said authorities did not investigate her for espionage. Megaspeed said she left in August 2025. Investigations into Megaspeed and six other individuals are ongoing. Wong said the chips were routed through Singapore to other countries, not to Singapore as a final destination, and that Singapore is also looking at other firms that may be rerouting chips. Albanese said Australia is not a party to the arrangements under investigation. Source: [sg.news.yahoo.com](https://sg.news.yahoo.com/pore-working-us-chip-export-043621603.html) · [suaragarut.id](https://suaragarut.id/en/singapore-megaspeed-chip-export-probe) · [limapagi.id](https://www.limapagi.id/en/singapore-megaspeed-chip-export-investigation)

**Anwar: US chip export controls will not hinder Malaysia’s cooperation with China: Zaobao**
Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim told the South China Morning Post that US export controls aimed at restricting China’s use of advanced AI chips will not stop Malaysia from cooperating with Beijing and Chinese companies. He said Malaysia is not siding with either China or the United States, that China had not raised concerns about Malaysia’s US ties, and that Malaysia will monitor whether companies with US ties ship chips to China, just as it monitors Chinese firms that must follow Beijing’s rules. He said a US rule that US companies cannot export to China is an agreement with those companies and Malaysia will comply, and that this will not stop Malaysia from accepting Chinese investment or working with Chinese companies. He also said foreign investors who want government help securing their supply chains will have to pay for that help. Source: [zaobao.com.sg](https://www.zaobao.com.sg/en/news/sea/anwar-us-chip-export-controls-will-not-hinder-malaysias-cooperation-china)

### Also Today
**Fujitsu's 2nm Monaka Chip Sees Order Surge, Rushes to Secure More TSMC Capacity: BigGo Finance**
Fujitsu’s 2-nanometer Monaka chip is seeing an order surge, and the company is rushing to secure more TSMC capacity. Source: [finance.biggo.com](https://finance.biggo.com/news/ca0bbc6d-55ae-42dc-81b0-d6bcace402f5)

**Harvard Leads $12M DOE Project on AI-Driven Quantum Error Correction: HPCwire**
Harvard’s Mikhail Lukin is leading a $12 million Department of Energy project on AI-driven quantum error correction that includes MIT, Cornell, three national labs, and tech partners, as part of the Genesis Mission. Source: [hpcwire.com](https://www.hpcwire.com/off-the-wire/harvard-leads-12m-doe-project-on-ai-driven-quantum-error-correction/)

**Intel Spotlights Amazon EC2 Instances Powered by Xeon at AWS re:Invent: Intel**
Intel pointed to Amazon EC2 instances powered by custom Intel Xeon processors for AI agents and mission-critical applications, and pointed customers to AWS re:Invent. Source: [x.com](https://x.com/intel/status/2124910852461490297)

### The Teardown: The Shorter Description That Still Has to Close Timing
High-level synthesis starts from a short, untimed description and emits register-transfer logic that a later flow can place, route, and time. In Semiconductor Engineering, Stuart Clubb of Siemens EDA puts the tool on the blocks that are too slow or too power-hungry to stay on a CPU, and that have not already been done as reusable IP. A bus interface or a peripheral, he says, is more likely to be IP reuse. HLS got pushed toward the new blocks: problems that had not been tackled, where someone still has to choose an architecture in hardware.

The productivity number in that same piece comes from Badru Agarwala of Rise Design Automation. HLS handles complex control and datapath with ten to twenty times less code than RTL. Less code is easier to review, which is how he says you come to trust what you ship, and easier to edit when the specification changes. That is the scaling claim: one block or a large subsystem, whether a person or an AI writes the description.

Amdahl’s law is the brake he puts on that claim. Writing RTL was never the biggest bottleneck. Making one relatively small part of development dramatically faster does not move the schedule much if the rest stays put. Most of the schedule, he says, is verification and the iterations needed to meet performance, power, and area. The offset he names is that verification of C is orders of magnitude faster than verification of RTL, and that HLS can synthesize quickly, so an agent can evaluate many alternatives in a short time. He also says that coupling is not here yet.

Diptesh Nandi of Microchip draws the boundary in power, not in lines of code. The goal is not to do everything in HLS, and not to do everything as a language model emitting RTL. Some portion of a design is there for time to market. If you use HLS, he says, it is probably going to consume more power because it is not going to be optimized the way hand-crafted RTL is. His FPGA picture of the flow is a path into a device, not a claim that every block belongs on it. The same article has Tom De Muer of Keysight EDA ordering the stack: software is leading, digital design is next, then mixed analog, then full physics, and high-level synthesis sits in the digital part, lagging software. His constraint on prompting is specific to this industry: you cannot prompt something very vague and expect something production-ready, because a vague prompt does not carry the context a tape-out needs.

Trust is the older constraint, and it is why the shorter description does not retire the engineer. Dave Kelf of Breker Verification Systems says HLS now has real value for a specific segment, and that a historic barrier — the same one logic synthesis once had — was the disconnect between the abstract model, especially circuit timing, and the final design. Engineers had trouble making that connection, and that made them nervous about trusting the result. De Muer puts a field failure next to a clean lab result: a design can pass a full one-hundred-percent regression and still fail in the field, and then someone has to understand how it works in order to fix it. He says it took a long time before HLS was trusted, because people in that seat have been burned by things they did not understand.

The rules that keep the output recognizable have been stable. Clubb says the synthesizable subset of C++, and by extension SystemC, has stayed relatively constant for the last ten to fifteen years. Modeling streaming interfaces in an untimed sequential language needed IP, because the language does not show explicit concurrency. Siemens created AC channel and bit-accurate data types so that streaming could be represented inside that subset. Mehir Arora of ChipAgents reads the whole climb as a bargain: for fifty years, EDA progress meant climbing abstraction — RTL, then HLS — because a person cannot hold the full design space. Abstraction narrows the space so an engineer can reason about it, and that narrowing is a loss of potential quality of result. HLS, in his line, was never about better hardware. It was the price of designing for human capacity.

Walk the article’s own ratio through a block that is new enough to miss the IP shelf. The description is ten to twenty times shorter than the RTL it replaces, so review and a spec change land on the short text. C-level checks, orders of magnitude faster than RTL checks, are what would let an agent try architectures before a netlist exists. The output still has to be implementable RTL that meets power, performance, and area inside a defined context. Nandi’s comparison is the bill on that last step: the HLS result is the one that was not hand-optimized, so the power is the higher one relative to crafted RTL. If the block was a bus or a peripheral, Clubb’s path never entered this flow. IP reuse was the likely answer, and the ten-to-twenty-times saving was never available because the code was not going to be written either way.

The choice stops being the right one when the repair has to be done by a person who cannot see from the short description to the timed circuit. De Muer’s one-hundred-percent regression that still fails in the field is that moment: the abstraction has already shipped, and the fix needs the connection Kelf says engineers have always had trouble making. It also stops when the power envelope cannot take Nandi’s unoptimized result, and when a generator wants to leave the synthesizable subset Clubb says has been stable for ten to fifteen years. Outside that subset, the output is no longer the circuit the ten-to-fifteen-year rules taught an engineer to recognize, and Arora’s fifty-year bargain — a smaller space, held by a person — no longer covers the repair. Source: [semiengineering.com](https://semiengineering.com/ai-vs-high-level-synthesis/)

### On the Horizon
- Public comments on the US Commerce Department interim final rule “Addressing Remote Access to Advanced Semiconductors,” which took effect November 19, 2026, are due January 19, 2027.
- Jensen Huang and Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter are scheduled for closed-door interviews with US congressional committees examining the Megaspeed chip case; the reports do not give the day.

# AI Chips & Data Centres Daily
> **Nearly twenty fabs of tool demand still chase AI orders clients have not cut.**

**What You Need to Know:** TSMC senior vice president Cliff Hou said on November 23 that clients have not adjusted planned orders, and he has put AI-tied equipment demand at nearly the equivalent of building 20 new fabs at once, even as the foundry tightens credit. The same day TSMC publicly said advanced-process capacity is still short of demand. Intel, separately, has a first outside customer for 18A-P.

### Top Story
TSMC says advanced-process orders are still being placed as planned, and that the tool build behind them has not shrunk with the market's AI doubts.

On November 23, senior vice president Cliff Hou said clients have not adjusted their orders. He has also described AI-related equipment demand as nearly equivalent to building 20 new fabs simultaneously. The same day the company issued a public statement that global AI demand is still growing, that its long-term outlook stays positive, and that advanced-process capacity falling short of demand continues. It separated that from consumer electronics, where it acknowledged rising component prices and macroeconomic uncertainty.

The credit side moved the other way. Between November 18 and 20, TSMC began reviewing customer balance sheets and setting stricter credit limits, with the tighter look falling most heavily on custom AI chip buyers, the ASIC customers. Orders above those limits may have to be paid in cash upfront. As of June 2026 the company held NT$234 billion in customer prepayments. Hou's account is that orders are unchanged and the credit terms are tighter. Source: [cryptobriefing.com](https://cryptobriefing.com/tsmc-cliff-hou-no-order-adjustments/) Source: [finance.biggo.com](https://finance.biggo.com/news/acd6c285-f4b8-4557-9be1-1ca5684ccae4)

### Silicon
**Intel lands an unnamed outside customer for 18A-P:** TechPowerUp
Intel chief executive Lip-Bu Tan said the company has signed its first outside customer for 18A, speaking at the TomorrowX Summit in Austin; chief technology officer Pushkar Ranade later confirmed on X that the deal is for 18A-P specifically. That node entered risk production in June. Intel claims 9 percent higher performance at the same power, or 18 percent lower power at the same performance, versus 18A, and says 18A-P is design-rule compatible with 18A. Tan has confirmed Nova Lake will use 18A-P internally. Socionext said in August it would use 18A-P for custom SoCs, so the "first" label is in dispute; TechPowerUp notes this may be the first signed manufacturing deal. Attendees quoted Tan as saying 18A yields are now at 70 percent; TechPowerUp says those reports are unconfirmed. Source: [techpowerup.com](https://www.techpowerup.com/355094/intel-lands-an-unnamed-external-customer-for-its-18a-p-node)

**Centec ZX530S-24S2CQ review, a cheap 10G and 100G switch:** ServeTheHome
ServeTheHome bought a switch for $500 and found sixth-generation switch silicon from Chinese vendor Centec inside. The box is a 24-port SFP+ 10G switch with two 100G SFP28 ports, the ZX530S-24S2CQ. The lab ran it on a high-end Keysight IxNetwork setup. Source: [servethehome.com](https://www.servethehome.com/centec-zx530s-24s2cq-review/) Source: [youtube.com](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=f-5PGy8gt8o&feature=youtu.be)

### Data Centres & Power
**Lenders back a $43 billion Nvidia GPU deal and worry about orbit:** Tom's Hardware
Tom's Hardware reports lenders are backing SpaceX's $43 billion Nvidia GPU deal but worry the collateral could end up in orbit and be impossible to reclaim in a default. The loan is structured so a different company buys the Nvidia chips while SpaceX makes quarterly payments to use them. The five-year hell-or-high-water lease may lack a written earth-only guarantee. Source: [tomshardware.com](https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/data-centers/lenders-back-spacexs-usd43-billion-nvidia-gpu-deal-but-worry-the-collateral-could-end-up-in-orbit-making-it-impossible-to-reclaim-if-musk-defaults-five-year-hell-or-high-water-lease-may-lack-a-written-earth-only-guarantee)

### Supply Chain & Policy
**SoftBank's $1 trillion SK hynix look is no longer active:** EE Times
The Information reported on November 20 that SoftBank chief executive Masayoshi Son recently explored a $1 trillion buyout of SK hynix. A SoftBank spokesperson said the company explores many opportunities and this one is no longer under active consideration. SK hynix said it had no knowledge of the matter and that any outreach was entirely on the SoftBank side. EE Times reports there were no negotiations and no term sheet. The floated price is 1.7 times SK hynix's $577 billion market valuation recorded that Friday. EE Times treats financing, chaebol governance, and Seoul's view of memory as a strategic asset as the hurdles that would have stopped a close. On SoftBank's own map the empty layer is memory: it has Arm, Graphcore (2024), Ampere (2025), a stake in Intel, a large OpenAI commitment, nearly $500 billion into Stargate and the DigitalBridge acquisition, and is the largest shareholder in SB Energy. SK hynix's HBM revenue more than doubled year on year in 2025. Nvidia was 14.8 percent of SK hynix revenue in the first quarter of 2026, and TrendForce expects Nvidia to place about two-thirds of its HBM4 orders with SK hynix. Source: [eetimes.com](https://www.eetimes.com/the-enigma-of-softbanks-1-trillion-sk-hynix-buyout-attempt/)

**Eternal Materials' advanced packaging materials start showing up in profit:** BigGo Finance
Eternal Materials reported preliminary October pretax profit of NT$254 million, about $7.7 million, up 99.31 percent year on year, with pretax earnings per share of NT$0.19. Pretax profit for the first ten months was NT$2.937 billion, about $89.4 million, up 50.70 percent, with pretax EPS of NT$2.4. October revenue was NT$4.058 billion, about $123.5 million, down 8.47 percent from September and up 30.82 percent from a year earlier. The company tied the monthly drop to fewer working days and China's National Day holiday. Shipments of synthetic resins, specialty materials, and dry film photoresist fell with the holiday; precision equipment and advanced packaging materials stayed at high levels. October pretax profit fell about 34 percent from September. For the fourth quarter the company said traditional resins and general electronic materials should be flat to slightly below the third quarter, while semiconductor packaging materials and precision equipment remain a peak-season contributor, with precision equipment in intensive customer acceptance. Source: [finance.biggo.com](https://finance.biggo.com/news/77fe36d8-e463-4cf4-86ac-f88de80ef840)

**Treasury still has no Nvidia export answers as a House interview is set:** Tech Times
Days before a window Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent set on November 15, he said on CBS's Face the Nation that Treasury does not yet have answers on Nvidia export-control compliance, and that such responsibility normally sits with the legal department, the general counsel's office — at Nvidia, Tim Teter's. Bessent's "answers in the next 10 days" clock, counted from that November 15 broadcast, closes about November 25. Teter is scheduled for a closed-door interview with three House committees on December 2. The board announced an independent investigation on November 8 and, in a November 10 statement, said it retained Joon H. Kim of Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz. On November 17 Nvidia announced an export-control committee; the National Security Team and Global Trade Compliance Team now report to that committee and to interim chief executive Colette Kress day to day. Commerce's November 16 rule requires a license when a data center anywhere gives customers headquartered in China, or in other countries of concern, more than 12 million aggregate total processing performance; TechCrunch estimated that near 750 Nvidia H100 or H200 chips. The rule also requires licenses for covered chips shipped to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Brazil, with US-headquartered recipients exempt if they file monthly reports. Bessent said Nvidia took Megaspeed off its sales list in August 2025; Nvidia, and a Commerce and Justice Department joint statement, put the ban in June 2025. Source: [techtimes.com](https://www.techtimes.com/articles/331309/20261123/nvidia-export-controls-bessent-points-general-counsels-office-while-treasury-lacks-answers.htm)

### The Teardown: The Twenty-Second Bridge
A data-centre outage is a timing problem before it is a generation problem. The IT load has to stay powered across the gap between utility failure and the moment another source is actually carrying that load. Data Center Knowledge describes the traditional instrument for that gap as a centralized uninterruptible power supply: stored battery energy, plus voltage regulation, sized to the critical load. The publication puts a typical UPS bridge at 10 to 15 minutes. Operators replace those batteries every 3 to 5 years. As the facility's normal draw rises, UPS capacity has to rise with the critical load, so the same outage minute costs more battery, more floor area, and another replacement cycle.

Battery energy storage uses the same stored-energy idea at a different scale. Data Center Knowledge says a BESS can support loads for hours, depending on system size and configuration, against that 10-to-15-minute UPS window. The tradeoff it names is a higher upfront investment and more complex integration. The sites it points to are the ones that see longer outages, want to store renewable energy, or are building a more flexible on-site energy strategy. In that design the UPS need not be the only ride-through asset. It can sit as a complement.

Rack-level batteries move the short store into the rack. A centralized UPS, the publication says, can support dozens or even hundreds of servers from one installation, and it consumes floor space that could otherwise be used to raise density. Rack batteries localize protection and can cut the heat concentration of a battery room or a large UPS installation. They still need periodic replacement and lifecycle management. On the facts given, they do not turn a minute-scale bridge into an hour-scale one. They change where the minutes live.

Buffer modules are the short end of the same clock. Historically they bridged milliseconds of downtime or a voltage dip. Newer systems, Data Center Knowledge says, can cover up to 20 seconds — long enough in some cases to cover startup of a diesel generator or another on-site source. If the design goal is only to hold servers until that transfer, the publication treats the buffer as a possible replacement for a full UPS, and calls it a lower-cost, lower-maintenance option. It does not claim the buffer regulates voltage across a 15-minute outage. Twenty seconds is the design window, not a smaller UPS.

On-site microgrids change what the transfer lands on. If generation is already able to serve a substantial share of the load on an ongoing basis, the preferred response to a grid break can be a transfer to local power rather than a long battery bridge. Data Center Knowledge says that, with enough capacity and redundancy, a microgrid can reduce reliance on large centralized UPS systems for extended backup. It also says microgrids do not automatically eliminate power conditioning or ride-through protection.

Walk the clock with only those figures. A grid break starts it. If the plan is generator start, the buffer's 20 seconds is the whole budget the publication is willing to treat as enough. If the plan is the traditional UPS, the budget is 10 to 15 minutes, and the batteries behind it are on a 3-to-5-year replacement cycle. If the plan is a BESS, the contrast the publication draws is hours rather than those minutes, paid for with a higher upfront cost and a harder integration. The centralized UPS still occupies floor that could have held the servers — dozens or hundreds of them — whose density the operator is trying to raise. The hybrid the publication calls the practical path keeps a short ride-through, buffer or UPS, in front of whichever longer asset, BESS or microgrid, is supposed to take the load after the transfer.

The centralized UPS stops being the right primary design when the outage being bridged is either much shorter than its 10-to-15-minute rating or much longer than a battery room the operator is willing to replace every 3 to 5 years. If on-site generation is the real source and it is online inside 20 seconds, Data Center Knowledge's own comparison points at the buffer, not the UPS hall. If the outage runs for hours and the site is already storing energy for renewables or flexibility, the same comparison points at the BESS. What still forces a UPS, or something that does its conditioning job, to stay in the path is the limit the publication states at the end: a transfer onto a microgrid leaves voltage regulation and a short ride-through unsolved. Source: [datacenterknowledge.com](https://www.datacenterknowledge.com/uptime/emerging-alternatives-to-ups-in-data-centers)

### On the Horizon
- About November 25: the 10-day window Bessent set on November 15 for Nvidia's board and outside counsel to deliver export-compliance answers.
- December 2: Tim Teter's closed-door interview with three House committees.

# AI Chips & Data Centres Daily
> **Sixteen months after working transistors, Rapidus still has no SRAM for 2027.**

**What You Need to Know:** Sixteen months after Rapidus showed working two-nanometre transistors, it still has no functioning SRAM, and a 2027 mass-production start is at risk. Nvidia has now named a science accelerator, Rubin HPC, with more than 50,000 CUDA cores and a 2028 arrival. Treasury says older-chip rules need no further tightening, while a House tally counts 879,868 Nvidia and AMD chips already licensed toward Chinese-tied buyers.

### Top Story
Rapidus has missed a summer target to show a working SRAM cell on its two-nanometre-class gate-all-around process, and Tom's Hardware, drawing on Bloomberg, reports that the government-backed startup has not produced functioning static random-access memory cells. The company did make test structures with gate-all-around transistors at its IIM-1 fab in Hokkaido in July 2025; chief executive Atsuyoshi Koikem told Hot Chips 2025 that on July 10 those transistors showed the expected electrical characteristics. A single working transistor is a much smaller circuit than a six-transistor SRAM bitcell with contacts, wordlines, bitlines and power rails, and SRAM arrays are how process teams usually expose defects and variability before a real processor will yield. The same report says Rapidus is also fighting contamination in its cleanroom. In a Japan Times interview, Rapidus said it was on track to mass-produce chips in the second half of fiscal 2027, which ends on March 31, 2028; earlier targets had been stated without separating fiscal years from calendar years. For scale, Tom's Hardware notes that TSMC's N2 showed more than 50 percent yield on a 256-megabit SRAM test chip in April 2023, more than 80 percent SRAM yield by April 2024, and over 90 percent average yield on that vehicle by May 2025, about half a year before mass production. Only Intel, TSMC and Samsung have begun mass production on nodes that use gate-all-around devices. Source: [tomshardware.com](https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/semiconductors/rapidus-reportedly-struggles-to-produce-working-sram-on-its-2nm-node-putting-2027-mass-production-at-risk-company-faces-significant-challenges-using-euv-to-develop-gaa-transistors)

### Silicon
**Nvidia unveils Rubin HPC GPU with more than 50,000 CUDA cores, expected in 2028: Mezha**
Nvidia announced Rubin HPC at the SC26 supercomputing conference as an accelerator for scientific simulation and data analysis, not for consumer graphics, and expects it in deployed systems in 2028. The chip has more than 50,000 CUDA cores in one GPU, against 21,760 CUDA cores in the GeForce RTX 5090, which Mezha describes as almost three times as many. It joins the Vera Rubin platform. Nvidia says the design pairs that core count with faster data movement so units spend less time waiting, and it adds sparse-data acceleration for sparse matrices, stencil calculations, sorting and reduction. The accelerator uses seventh-generation NVLink for GPU-to-GPU communication. Ian Buck, vice president of hyperscale and high-performance computing, said: "For agents tackling science and engineering, faster simulation means faster discovery." Independent testing has not established how much faster specific workloads will run. The part is announced, not shipping. Source: [mezha.net](https://mezha.net/eng/news/mezha-ef50243c0beadc952a973cde_nvidia_unveils_rubin/)

**Phison Previews an SSD That Runs AI Frameworks on Its Own NPU: TechPowerUp**
At SC26 in Chicago, Phison showed a computational-storage design, still in development and presented as a proof of concept, that puts an NPU and 64 GB of onboard memory running at 130 GB/s on the drive and supports PyTorch, vLLM and OpenVINO. Phison says suitable workloads could cut data transfers by 10 to 100 times, because the drive scans and processes the dataset in parallel and returns results instead of the whole set. It rates the NPU in DMIPS rather than TOPS. At the same event, a mixed-media design puts high-endurance pSLC and QLC behind one 16-channel controller so a dedicated cache drive is not required; Phison says losing one drive in a 24-drive server would cost 4 percent of the cache instead of the usual 25 percent. The showcase also included a PCIe Gen 6 X3 controller first shown at Computex. Source: [techpowerup.com](https://www.techpowerup.com/355089/phison-previews-an-ssd-that-runs-ai-frameworks-on-its-own-npu)

**AMD grabs over 40% of new TOP500 list for supercomputers, up 14% since last year: Tom's Hardware**
Tom's Hardware's SC26 roundup says AMD is now in over 40 percent of the new TOP500 list, up 14 percent since last year. Lux, built with the U.S. Department of Energy, debuts at number 14 with EPYC CPUs and Instinct MI355X GPUs. A second machine, Discovery, is expected in 2028 with EPYC CPUs and Instinct accelerators. The top 10 systems are unchanged: China's LineShine system in Shenzhen remains first, and El Capitan remains second. The list recorded the fewest new systems in 33 years, which the roundup ties to AI data centres soaking up new hardware that is not being run on the TOP500 benchmark. Source: [tomshardware.com](https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/supercomputers/this-week-on-toms-hardware-premium-21-november-2026-amd-nvidia-and-more-show-off-the-future-of-high-performance-computing-at-sc26)

### Data Centres & Power
**Trump wants to ban US companies from building overseas data centers as bans slow development: Tom's Hardware**
President Donald Trump said he wants to stop U.S. companies from building data centres in other countries, or to charge a "tremendous tax" if they proceed, and Tom's Hardware, citing Axios, reports he has not discussed the idea with his cabinet. He said, "They're making so much money they don't know what to do with it," and, "We're not allowing data centers to go into other countries because China will take all of them, and we're not allowing that to happen." Moratoriums on data centres have surged past 500 across the United States. A Pennsylvania town has listed 43 specific demands for one project; New York State has recommended that municipalities seek 1 million dollars of community investment per megawatt; one developer has offered 10,000 dollars per household; SpaceX is buying 418 homes near a flagship AI data centre. The House passed the Remote Access Security Act in January 2026 to close overseas-compute workarounds; the bill remains in the Senate. Nvidia has warned clients that customers should be at least 51 percent not from China. Congress, not the White House, imposes federal taxes, and the opposing party controls both chambers. A ban would also collide with foreign data-residency rules and would lengthen latency for users outside the United States. Source: [tomshardware.com](https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/data-centers/trump-wants-to-ban-us-companies-from-building-overseas-data-centers-as-bans-slow-development-also-considers-putting-a-tremendous-tax-in-lieu-of-prohibition)

### Supply Chain & Policy
**Bessent says no further restrictions are needed for Nvidia chip exports to China: PBS**
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Friday that no further restrictions are needed on sales of older Nvidia chips to China, and that remote access has been curtailed, after Jensen Huang stepped down amid allegations involving Megaspeed. A day earlier, the House Foreign Affairs Committee released Commerce Department licensing detail: as of May 11, 2026, the Bureau of Industry and Security had approved export, re-export or transfer of 879,868 Nvidia H200 and AMD MI325X chips to Chinese-tied companies across 21 applications, out of more than 3.4 million chips requested. Approvals are not completed sales. The count includes 75,000 for Alibaba, 150,000 for Tencent and its subsidiaries, 43,000 for Baidu and 4,000 for BYD, companies the Defense Department has identified as tied to the Chinese military. BIS said the approach follows a Federal Register rule published in January and that it has a long record of telling Congress about H200 licensing, including rejections. Nvidia said the limited H200 shipments it made were legal and authorized, that review took more than half a year, and that it is no longer shipping H200 chips to China despite prior approvals. AMD said it complies with U.S. export rules. Bessent has publicly faulted Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick over delay on Megaspeed controls; President Trump said Friday he has not lost confidence in Lutnick. Source: [pbs.org](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/bessent-says-no-further-restrictions-are-needed-for-nvidia-chip-exports-to-china)

**Samsung, SK hynix face AI memory doubts despite record profits as shares slide: Korea JoongAng Daily**
SemiAnalysis cut its forecast for global HBM bit demand in 2028 by about 30 percent and cut that year's AI-accelerator spending from 1.054 trillion dollars to 758 billion dollars, while UBS estimates that about 30 percent of new U.S. data-centre capacity expected in 2028 faces regulatory risk. Even that lower path still has accelerator spending up about 21 percent in 2028 from 627 billion dollars in 2027, with HBM bit demand still growing each year. After Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia's chief executive on November 12, Nvidia forecast fourth-quarter revenue of 130 billion dollars, above expectations of 125.1 billion dollars, and raised its fiscal 2028 revenue-growth forecast to 75 percent from 70 percent. SK hynix's largest customer, presumed to be Nvidia, accounted for 34.98 trillion won (26.2 billion dollars) in the first nine months, 14.8 percent of sales, down from 27 percent a year earlier, even as sales to that customer doubled; a second customer is now 10.1 percent, or 23.9 trillion won. Alphabet and Amazon appear among Samsung's five biggest customers, together about 24 percent of sales, and Nvidia is not on that list. Kim Dong-won of KB Securities estimates Nvidia at 38 percent of global HBM demand in 2027, Google at 37 percent and AMD at 13 percent. Kim Yong-kwan of Samsung put neoclouds at about 8 percent of the market. Samsung has effectively sold out next year's HBM supply, and SK hynix says long-term contracts lock more than 50 percent of capacity for 2027 and 2028, but both say volumes and delivery periods can change with demand, and Nvidia has told the SEC that some supply commitments can be canceled or rescheduled before formal orders. SK hynix said last month that DRAM and HBM output is effectively sold out through 2029, counting signed contracts and demand still under negotiation. Source: [koreajoongangdaily.com](https://www.koreajoongangdaily.com/business/samsung-sk-hynix-face-ai-memory-doubts-despite-record-profits-as-shares-slide/12984231)

### Also Today
**Intel Nova Lake-H Spec Sheet Shows Up With a 4.8 GHz Boost and 25 W TDP: TechPowerUp**
Advantech's preliminary datasheet for the ASR-A505 robot board lists a 16-core Core Ultra Series 4 Nova Lake-H part at a 4.8 GHz boost, a 2.0 GHz P-core base, 18 MB of last-level cache and a 25 W TDP, labeled 8P+4E+4LE against earlier leaks of a 4P+8E+4LPE Ultra 9 4970H. Source: [techpowerup.com](https://www.techpowerup.com/355088/intel-nova-lake-h-spec-sheet-shows-up-with-a-4-8-ghz-boost-and-25-w-tdp)

**28-Core Intel "Nova Lake-S" Appears in Testing Running at 5.2 GHz: TechPowerUp**
OpenBenchmark shows an engineering sample named Intel 0000 with an NVL identifier, a 28-core configuration and a 5.2 GHz figure that is not confirmation of a final retail boost clock. Source: [techpowerup.com](https://www.techpowerup.com/355078/28-core-intel-nova-lake-s-appears-in-testing-running-at-5-2-ghz)

### The Teardown: Charge on the Gate, Not on a Capacitor
A Z2RAM cell holds its bit as charge on the gate of a read transistor, and that read does not empty the charge. IEEE Spectrum describes the prototype from Nagare Labs, spun out of Georgia Tech by Suman Datta and Shimeng Yu. A conventional DRAM cell stores the bit as charge on a capacitor. The act of reading drains the capacitor, so the array must write the bit back before it can be trusted again. Datta puts that write-back loop at 40 to 50 nanoseconds. Z2RAM throws out the capacitor and uses two transistors. One writes. The other reads without disturbing what was stored, so read and write no longer share a single port the way they do when every read forces a restore. Charge sitting on the read transistor's gate also amplifies the signal, which means a smaller stored charge can still be sensed quickly. Datta's best-case estimate for that read is one to two nanoseconds. SRAM remains the faster cell, because it is built in the same front-end process as the processor it serves. It is also the expensive cell: every extra bit competes for area on a logic die, and the SRAM cell has proved hard to shrink.

The density argument is vertical. Datta says the memory transistors can be built with plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition at less than 450 degrees Celsius, cool enough to add layers on a finished CMOS wafer without degrading it. Nagare's plan is to tape out the control circuits first on a mature logic process, build the array above them with multiple layers per lithography step, and bond the finished chip onto a processor as a chiplet. The first generation targets six layers and 185 megabits per square millimeter, about five times what SRAM achieves. Datta projects that the same approach could eventually stack up to 106 layers, which would put density at about 90 times SRAM. Take the near-term claim first. Six layers and five times SRAM is the number a customer could be asked to design around. The 90-times figure is not six layers repeated; it is the same cell carried to 106 layers, a stack more than seventeen times as tall as generation one, and the article does not publish a per-layer bit count a buyer could multiply alone. A patented metal shield inside each cell is there because the write transistor, when it switches off, couples into the stored charge and narrows the margin the read needs. The shield separates the two devices. It also makes each cell wider. Stacking is how Nagare expects to earn that width back.

This added layer stops being the right one on the package when the voltage that turns those oxide transistors on drifts under bias and temperature. Datta calls threshold-voltage stability the biggest challenge for this class of device. If that turn-on point moves, a stored bit is misread. The shield does not restore a threshold that walked, and another deposited layer copies the same film. Nagare is still tuning indium and gallium oxides, sometimes with zinc, and tungsten-doped indium oxide. There is also no agreed way to attach this memory to an AI chip; Datta's opening is only that high-bandwidth memory for accelerators is already moving from standard parts toward custom ones. Gelsinger's gate, before any of that attach work counts, is a device out of the university lab, a fabrication partner, and a demonstration on standard production wafers. Until a returned wafer holds its threshold, the one-to-two-nanosecond read remains a cell estimate, not a latency a scheduler can book. Source: [spectrum.ieee.org](https://spectrum.ieee.org/sram-memory-z2ram)

### On the Horizon
- Nvidia expects Rubin HPC in deployed systems in 2028.
- Discovery, the second AMD system named in the TOP500 roundup, is expected to debut in 2028 with EPYC CPUs and Instinct accelerators.
- Rapidus told the Japan Times it is aiming at mass production in the second half of fiscal 2027, a window that ends on March 31, 2028.
